Citi Internship Process Experience-
Aishwarya Ravi B Tech Electronics
Eligibility Criteria:

CGPA: 6.5

Eligible Branches: CS, IT and Circuit branches

Active Backlogs: No

Dead Backlogs: Yes
Stipend: INR 75,000 per month
Role: PBWMT(Personal Banking and Wealth Management Tech)
The entire process was divided in the following rounds:

Online Test Round ( 1hr 15 minutes)

Interview Rounds:
Technical Round ( 50minutes )
HR Round ( 45 minutes )
Online Coding Round
The coding round was hosted on the SHL platform. After clicking on the
test initiation link, I was redirected to an identification window, where I
had to take a picture with my government ID. Following that, I was
instructed to fill in some details and I entered the test window. The
entire test was proctored so we had to keep our videos and mics on and

fully functional throughout the duration of the test. Make sure you
properly check your test environment beforehand which includes
Chrome Version, video cam and mic compatibility and a stable internet
connection. In the test, There were following sections:

Automata ( 2 coding Questions in 45minutes )

SQL ( 12 multiple-choice Questions in 15minutes )

ReactJS ( 12Q multiple-choice Questions in 15minutes )

Angular6 ( 12Q multiple-choice Questions in 15minutes )
Automata Section:
This section consisted of two coding questions and duration allotted
was 45minutes. The first problem was pretty simple and straight
forward, you were given an array of integers and you had to sort the first
half in ascending order and the second half in descending order and
return the resulting sorted array. I was able to solve this within 10
minutes and passed all 7/7 test cases. But as soon as I tried navigating to
the second question from the side bar menu, the test got auto-
submitted, it could’ve been due to platform incompatibility or my
unstable internet connection, So I can’t help you with the second
question since I myself didn’t get the chance to see that. I was
disheartened when this happened because I had 35 minutes in total in
which I could’ve easily solved the problem but it was unfortunate, I
chose to attempt the next set of sections.
SQL:
In this section, you were asked to select the correct query for given
problem statements, It was a pretty easy section, be thorough with
CRUD operations, DDL, DML, Data Constraints, Join queries, just have a
good hold on basic SQL syntax and you’re good to go.
ReactJS:
If you are a web developer, this is a section that you can ace easily.
There were questions regarding reusable components, state
management, React Hooks, Choose the correct statements among these,
find the missing attribute in the given code snippets, output based.
AngularJS:
I had no idea about this framework except for basic installation
commands so this section was pretty much guess work from my end,
also we were not expecting this section in the test so in true sense
nobody was actually prepared for this section.

Interview Round
Technical Round (10:00am-10:50am)
1) My interview was scheduled on 4th Sept at 10:00am on Zoom. The
shortlisted candidates were allotted the Zoom ID and Password in the
spreadsheet along with the details of the panelist. I logged in sharp at
10am, make sure you’re on time, it reflects punctuality.
2) The panelist was one of the VP of Citi India and I did some background
check on him through LinkedIn, I would suggest you to do that, you
would then have an idea about which frameworks has he worked on and
the ones which align with your profile, its very likely that he would
continue the discussion on those topics only.
Citi prefers candidates who are proficient in Web Development, DBMS
and JAVA.
3) As soon as I entered the meeting room, I started off by greeting him
and then he proceeded to ask me for a brief introduction. Try to keep
your introductions under 1 minute and cover your academics,
technologies and frameworks you have worked on.
4) He then dedicated a full minute in going through my Resume and the
Tech stack that was associated with my major projects, he started with
ReactJS. Asked me how well I know about front-end frameworks and
why did I choose ReactJS over VanillaJS.
I covered 3-4 points about why did I prefer ReactJS which included the
efficient state management feature, virtual DOM(explained it with an
example) and reusable components. I also mentioned about React
Native for MobileApps. He was satisfied with the answer. He proceeded
to ask me a follow-up question if I knew AngularJS, I was honest and I
said I haven’t worked on it. He asked how can we use these reusable
components outside of ReactJS. He seemed satisfied with my response.
5) Next was DBMS, he asked me about the databases I’ve worked on, I
mentioned MongoDB and MySQL. He asked me why did I use MongoDB
instead of MySQL. And the discussion continued for another 7-8 minutes,
covering areas of relational databases and situation-based questions,

proceeded to APIs, servers and GraphQL, and how a specific database is
superior than the other in accordance with the demands of any platform.
He asked a query in MySQL and the features of MongoDB and how
would you write a schema and we also discussed about the
asynchronous nature of JS.
6) He then shifted the center of discussion to all my projects, he asked
me to explain in detail the features and how they were implemented, I
shared my screen and gave him a live demo of how the platform works
and what all features are included keeping the user experience as a
priority. He was intrigued by the Blockchain aspect of the project and
wanted me to explain web3 to him and how Blockchain Technology and
Smart Contracts execution works. He then asked me about the
difficulties I faced while working on the project and how did I overcome
those hurdles, if this project has any out-of-the-box element and is it
innovative enough to hold future potential. He proceeded to ask me to
pitch the platform infront of a client in order to convince him to
purchase the platform. I covered how this platform is one of its kind and
described about the business prospects. He completely saw the demo
asking questions every now and then regarding all the features.
Note: Please be thorough and confident with everything that you have
mentioned in your resume
Refrain from adding stuff that you are not confident on, they would
figure it out somehow that it is your weak point and would bombard you
with a series of questions that could make you nervous. Also, if in case
you fail to answer some questions during your interview, please be calm
and composed, keep an attitude where you’re willing to learn more
about it even if you have no idea at the moment about that tech. They
will test your patience and temperament during those times.
7) He then went on to ask some DSA questions(Linked list, array and
stacks), OOPs concepts and he concluded the interview.
“Do you have any questions?” I asked him about how his experience has
been in Citi, and that was it for the technical round.
I was positive about this round, within 10 minutes I got a call that I have
been shortlisted for the HR Round, new Zoom ID and password were
shared.
11/30 candidates were selected for the HR Round

HR Round (11:00am-11:50am)
The interviewer started the call late at around 11:10am, I was patiently
waiting for the meeting to start. It started with a normal “Hello
Aishwarya, how are you?” I greeted him back and then proceeded with
the introduction, during the entire duration his webcam was on and for
some reason it was enough to build a bit of pressure on me.
In my experience, this was the toughest and most nerve-wrecking round
in the entire process, coming immediately after undergoing 50 minutes
of Technical round, I was tired too since I didn’t get any break in
between to recollect myself.
1) Just like in the previous round, he took a lot of time in reading my
Resume, but this time he asked me about all the projects, including the
ones I implemented during hackathons (that would be 5 projects in
total), he went through each and every project and the tech stack
associated with it and tried understanding each and every feature and
implementation in great detail.
As I said, your resume is half your question paper for the interview.
Make sure you have a clear thought process and smooth flow while
you’re explaining them.
2) Next, I had mentioned that I am a full stack web developer in my intro,
so he asked me about front-end frameworks but was more focused on
the back-end technologies, Node and ExpressJS, I enjoyed discussing and
answering questions regarding it, because that’s the area I’m most
confident in and I decided to make the most out of this conversation.
The discussion started from basic Node and Express features, how the
server-side architecture works, how we define routes for our REST
APIs( Routing and HTTP Requests), Redux Toolkit, API payload, the
classic CORS error and how to fix it(headers, proxy server, extensions),
how the integration with database works. It was important for me to ace
this area because it aligned so much with the job profile that I applied
for. We went on discussing about how I used bcryptjs in hashing the
passwords and credentials,how the Authorization & Authentication
works.
3) He seemed extremely convinced with my answers, until he caught me
off-guard, he asked me about “Regular Expressions” concept in JS, I was
blank, I had an idea that it is used for validation purposes, but an idea

was not enough to take on that question. From this point on, my
interview went in a completely different direction and my chances of
getting selected became less. He asked me how would you make sure
that the user entered the correct format for an email if you don’t know
Regular Expressions? Instead of being quiet, I gave him a naive approach,
I mentioned using the validator.js library and apart from that, we can
add checks and edge cases to validate emails like mentioning @, popular
domain names, type=”email” in the input tag. He then realised I was
struggling, so he explained me about “Regular Expressions”, I managed
to seem devoted to what he was teaching me, but I lost a lot of my
confidence and composure there. The worst part was lined up just after
this, Do you know JAVA? I hesitated and answered, “Sir I have a basic
idea about it but I haven’t implemented it in any of my projects”. He was
visibly disappointed and I knew I am not going further in this process
because JAVA was such an important criteria in the selection process,
but I chose to remain honest about it.
4) Then we drifted towards discussing MySQL and MongoDB,the regular
drill, same set of questions from Round 1, post that he started
mentioning Databases that are used in companies and asked me about
databases being used in Meta, Instagram and other platforms, how they
work. Again, I had no idea about how those databases work at industry
level, there were some databases I heard for the first time, so that
section didn’t go well.
Now when I am writing all of this, I realise how critically he was judging
me and my personality, it wasn’t the fact that I couldn’t answer certain
questions, he was just trying to test my patience and how well I can take
things, how well can I maintain a positive mindset even after not being
able to respond well.
So, please don’t lose confidence and hope when its not going well,
interviewers don’t expect you to answer each and every question,
during that time they are just judging your character and how well you
can fit in the company.
5) For the final discussion, he chose Python, he asked some basic
programming logic questions, DSA (Linked List, Trees, Stacks), his prime
focus was on OOPs(Encapsulation, Abstraction, Polymorphism) along
with their types and proper examples. And with that the interview
ended.
I was among the 5 candidates selected for the internship.
All the best guys for your internship prep journey, you are going to ace it!
